newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dutch BNG looks to expand Asian funding.
newsitem.headline: Dutch BNG looks to expand Asian funding.

text.p: Dutch local authorities bank NV Bank Nederlandse Gemeenten (BNG), which has an annual funding requirement of US$7 billion, is looking to borrow more from Asian financial markets, BNG officials said in Singapore.
"BNG considers Asia to be its most important funding source after its European home market," Bert de Kock, Senior Vice-President Treasury for BNG said in a statement.
"We want to focus on Singapore in particular, as we are convinced that it has the same function in Southeast Asia as Switzerland has in Europe," he added.
The triple-A rated bank, which finances Dutch public authorities, is on a roadshow to introduce itself to Asian investors.
De Kock told a news conference BNG had already tapped the Japanese markets. "But for the future we cannot only rely on Europe and Japan."
He added that excluding Japan, BNG was looking to fund some 10 percent of its requirements in Asia within the next two to 2-1/2 years.
"The Dutch state issues no foreign debt. BNG is a good alternative. The Bank of Japan already regards BNG as a sovereign issuer," he said.
Although BNG debt does not carry the Dutch government's guarantee, de Kock described the bank as "a quasi-sovereign Dutch institution".
Bart van Dooren, head of International Capital Markets at BNG, said some 14 percent of BNG's funding is now in yen.
"We expect a substantial increase in our funding out of Japan -- maybe up to 20 percent on annual basis," he said.
De Kock said any borrowing in Asia was liable to be at the shorter end of the maturity spectrum. "For the time being...we're looking at short-term, up to five years," he said.
